title: FDA Clears First Blood Test Used in Diagnosing Alzheimer’s Disease | FDA
one_line: The FDA has granted clearance to the Lumipulse G pTau217/ß-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio, marking the first authorized blood-based in vitro diagnostic test for early detection of amyloid plaques in Alzheimer's disease.
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the Lumipulse G pTau217/ß-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio test developed by Fujirebio Diagnostics, Inc. This marks the first clearance of a blood-based in vitro diagnostic device to aid in diagnosing Alzheimer's disease. The test measures the ratio of pTau217 to beta-amyloid 1-42 in plasma, correlating to the presence of brain amyloid plaques and reducing the reliance on costly PET scans or invasive lumbar punctures. In a multi-center study of 499 cognitively impaired adults, the test demonstrated a 91.7% positive agreement and a 97.3% negative agreement with PET scan or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings. However, nearly 20% of the sample yielded indeterminate results. The FDA emphasizes that the blood test is not a standalone diagnostic tool and must be used in conjunction with other clinical evaluations.

key_claims.claim: The Lumipulse blood test reliably predicts the presence or absence of amyloid pathology associated with Alzheimer's disease.
key_claims.evidence: A clinical study of 499 cognitively impaired adults showed 91.7% positive agreement and 97.3% negative agreement with established amyloid PET scan or CSF test results.

key_claims.claim: The plasma ratio test reduces the need for PET scans and spinal taps while maintaining substantial equivalence.
key_claims.evidence: Requires only a simple blood draw and is substantially equivalent to the previously authorized Lumipulse G β-amyloid Ratio (1-42/1-40) test that uses cerebrospinal fluid.

methods.design: multi-center clinical validation study comparing plasma samples to PET/CSF results
methods.population: adults aged 55 and older who were cognitively impaired

limitations: Test is not a standalone diagnostic and must be interpreted alongside other clinical information
Risk of false positives leading to unnecessary treatment and distress
Risk of false negatives leading to delayed effective treatment
Nearly 20% of tests in the clinical study resulted in an indeterminate finding
red_flags: The press release mentions an indeterminate result rate of 'less than 20%' almost as an aside, which is a fairly high inconclusive rate for clinical application
Lacks demographic breakdowns of the 499-patient cohort, making it unclear if the test performs equally well across different ethnicities and comorbidities
